sundmay⚡️ Welcome to the world of electronics with Python that can interact with
electronics (it's called CircuitPython).

⚙️ Through a series of five 1.5 hour workshops, we will introduce you to
circuits with paper circuits, find out what breadboards are (It's not made of
bread 🍞). How it all connects together, what is a Raspberry Pi Pico, and how do
you use code to make it all work? And what is this CircuitPython you keep
mentioning?

🎮 By the last session, you will be able to code a game controller connected to
a Raspberry Pi Pico, and when you connect that a laptop, you can play games! And
as it's customisable, you can change and modify it as it's all in Python! 🐍

👉 Each session builds on the previous one, so it's advised to attend all the
sessions.

NOTE: There's only 10 places for this workshop.
We hope to see more folks from the underrepresented community to participate in
our workshop series.

🎟️ Register here:
https://ti.to/coding-grace/circuitpython-and-electronics-workshop-series
[https://ti.to/coding-grace/circuitpython-and-electronics-workshop-series]

🗓️ Workshop Dates

 * Session 1 - Intro to Circuits with Paper Circuits: Sat, Sep 5 (11:00 - 12:30)

 * Session 2 - A Taste of Electronics: Sat, Sep 12 (11:00 - 12:30)

 * Session 3 - A Taste of Pico: Sat, Sep 19 (11:00 - 12:30)

 * Session 4 - More with CircuitPython and Pico: Sat, Sep 26 (11:00 - 12:30)

 * Session 5 - ALT.CTRL GamePad: Sat, Oct 3 (11:00 - 12:30)
